why: 'which AS A PURE SUBSTANCE only exhibits a light floral jasmin-note' — the odour is attributed to the molecule in its own right, explicitly separated from the composition. 'reinforces diffusion, freshness and volume of a perfume composition' is a BLEND EFFECT and is not captured. 'light' is intensity. Hedione(R) is the trade name of the same compound and is not a second molecule.
Same sentence as n=1253 in a second patent family, 'jasmine note' rather than 'jasmin-note' — which is why dedupe did not merge them. Valid row, SAME MOLECULE.

TWO compounds sharing ONE description — REVIEW-RULES: add both, approve once. The 'alkyl cyclopentanones' preamble is the class; the two compounds are named specifically and described in their own right. '(or methyl dihydrojasmonate)' is an alias for methyl hydrojasmonate, recorded once under the resolvable name. 'strong' is intensity.

Names the molecule but asserts NOTE TIER and vapour pressure, not an odour quality. 'heart note' is position, which REVIEW-RULES excludes. This is the paper's note-tier negative result in the flesh — and it carries the VP figure that section 2.3 still lacks.
Ingredient enumeration — 'such common materials (e.g., hedione, galaxolide, etc.)'. 'base notes' is position. No odour attributed to anything.
'An ALKYL dihydrojasmonate' — alkyl is an unspecified group, so this is a family, not a compound. 'excellent smell intensity' is intensity plus judgement, not a descriptor.
Composition-level: 'Perfume E was a perfume having strong citrus-floral character'. Hedione appears in the ingredient list, not as the bearer of the odour.
